Shinchō Kōki: the bowstrings broke, Nobunaga was wounded in the elbow by a spear, he said 女はくるしからず、急ぎ罷り出でよ, the palace was set on fire, and he closed the storeroom door (納戸) from inside and committed seppuku
Shinchō Kōki: names of those killed (Yashiro Shōsuke, Ban Tarōzaemon, Ban Shōrin, Murata Kichigo; Mori Ran, Riki and Bō) and the guards from the front hall joining the defence of the palace
Tokitsune Kyōki entry for 6/2: hour of the Rabbit (卯刻), 'immediately' (則時ニ) Nobunaga killed, Nobutada holed up in the Shimo-gosho (Prince Sanehito's Nijō palace)
Honjō Sōemon memoir: written around Kan'ei 17 (1640), says he thought the target was Ieyasu, and the temple entrance was quiet
Frois: was not in Kyoto at the time; details of washing his face, the arrow, the naginata, the gunshot wound, two versions of how he died, and not a hair left (毛髪も残らず灰)
Mori Ran's given name was Nariyoshi; his father Mori Yoshinari was killed in battle in Ōmi; the 1582 land grant locations; his birth year is disputed
The Atsumori dance appears in Shinchō Kōki at Okehazama, not at Honnōji; the Yasuda Sakubei and paper-door (shōji) scenes come from later legends
The Kyoto church (Nanbanji) was near Honnōji; Ieyasu was in the Kamigata area (Sakai) at the time
Akechi's army marched from Kameyama in Tanba during the night and surrounded the temple around dawn; the date was Tenshō 10, 6/2
